content: We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) to produce target: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. This is a stilbene derivative: 4,4'-dimethoxystilbene? Actually structure: central C=C with each phenyl bearing OMe at para? SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. That's trans-1,2-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)ethene (p-methoxystyrene?). So we need a single-step synthesis from commercially available chemicals costing total <=150. Likely using Wittig reaction: combine p-anisaldehyde (4-methoxybenzaldehyde) with a phosphonium ylide (e.g., methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide) to give p-methoxystyrene? Actually Wittig of p-anisaldehyde with Ph3P=CH2 gives p-methoxystyrene (p-anisylmethylene). But we need bis(4-methoxyphenyl) ethene, i.e., coupling two aldehydes? Could use McMurry coupling of two p-anisaldehydes to give the alkene. That's a single step (McMurry reductive coupling). Starting material: 4-methoxybenzaldehyde (commercial). Reagent: TiCl4/Zn (McMurry) but reagents not counted as chemicals? Leaves must be commercially available chemicals; we can include reagents like TiCl4, Zn dust. Price likely under $150. So route: 2 equivalents of 4-methoxybenzaldehyde -> target via McMurry coupling (template: aldehyde dimerization to alkene). Need template ID for McMurry?
